figures.caption: A backward link $U$ and its forward inverse $u$ compare the same two fibers. Gauge factors cancel at the input and remain at the destination. The scalar example illustrates the exact transformation law.

The explicit finite coined walk supplies a current before a continuum interpretation is attempted. The plotted computation checks one-step local balance and total population for its declared finite data.
For Abelian links, the oriented edge phases cancel around adjacent faces. A holonomy is branch independent; a displayed real phase requires a branch choice.

Noncommuting $SU(2)$ factors retain their order. A based holonomy changes by conjugation, while the normalized Wilson trace is unchanged. The color fiber here is separate from the four-component Clifford spinor.
The four fine plaquettes are brought to common basepoints in a specified order. The exact cancellation leaves the eight outer links; a naive product omits the transport information.

For the specified constant generators, the finite calculation illustrates first-order raw curvature error and cancellation of its leading term. The analytic statement is Proposition~\ref{g:curvature-order}; a fitted slope over finitely many scales is a diagnostic of this example.

Integrated abelian phases compose exactly under edge subdivision. For the displayed coefficient $a(s)=\sin s$, the two subinterval integrals sum to the whole-edge integral. Independently sampled coarse and fine phases can disagree; that approximation error is separate from exact transport composition.

The selected five faces correspond to five adjacent swaps among the six corner paths. The sixth face is linked to them by the abelian cube Bianchi identity; it is not an independently omitted physical boundary condition.

A finite matrix illustration of the telescoping mechanism and the repeated-factor budget. The plotted common-space example tests the algebraic estimate; it is not an additional formal lattice-to-continuum theorem.

The non-affine background $A_y=\sin x$ has varying curvature and exact line-integral links. The quadratic envelope follows from $|\partial_xA_y|\leq1$; the computed phase amplitudes illustrate this bound over the plotted finite range.

For the regular connection envelope, halving the mesh quarters the one-level budget. The remaining accumulated error is bounded by the geometric tail $\frac43C4^{-n}$ once the adjacent-distance hypothesis has been established in a common complete space.

Eight equal children preserve a parent cell's total volume. Constant transported values use child volume weights; counting-normalized coefficients instead include the square root of the child volume. These are equivalent descriptions of the same Hilbert normalization.
